issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide(): String (UML and usage in Main call r.messageOnRide()), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implementations (Pig, Seal) implement the method with a String parameter. This parameter mismatch means students following the problem/template will implement a no-arg method but the solution uses a different signature, causing confusion and making it unclear which API is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: change the solution to match the problem/template by updating Rideable to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters) and modify Pig and Seal to implement the no-arg method, returning the required string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement UML, task descriptions, and template Main usage to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust example calls accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning a String (used as System.out.println(r.messageOnRide())). However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (and Pig/Seal implement this signature). This signature mismatch changes the intended API and output format, will cause the provided Main/template usage to not compile, and forces students to reconcile two different method signatures for the same conceptual operation (riding an animal).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API with the problem/template by removing the equipment parameter: change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [AnimalType] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template Main usage to call messageOnRide("<equipment>") and document the parameter, but prefer matching the problem (no-arg) to minimize student confusion.
